description: MATEØRBITA es un equipo independiente de Uruguay que combina curiosidad científica, pensamiento crítico e innovación tecnológica. Nos apasionan la astronomía, la matemática, la física y la ingeniería. Buscamos desarrollar soluciones creativas basadas en evidencia para afrontar los desafíos de la exploración espacial. Representamos el espíritu curioso y perseverante del sur, con la convicción de que las grandes ideas no tienen fronteras.
summary:
AnalogMatch is an interactive web platform designed to help explore and compare locations on Earth that can serve as analogs for studying the Moon and Mars. I developed a geographic explorer featuring 15 sites of interest, comparison tools, a recommender for potential analogs, a scientific scenario laboratory, and a case study focused on Arapey, Uruguay.

The project addresses this challenge by consolidating geological, climatic, and topographical information into a single space. It utilizes environmental data from services such as Open-Meteo/ERA5 and geological data from Macrostrat, while also providing access to scientific resources from NASA and the USGS. Furthermore, it incorporates an evaluation framework that enables the identification of evidence, data gaps, and uncertainties, while also defining the limits of similarity between Earth and other planetary bodies.

AnalogMatch aims to make planetary research more accessible, organized, and transparent, while demonstrating how terrestrial environments can help formulate new questions regarding space exploration.
details:
Project Details — AnalogMatch

AnalogMatch is an interactive web platform designed to investigate how specific environments on Earth can help us understand the geological, environmental, and topographical conditions of the Moon and Mars. Its goal is to facilitate the identification and analysis of potential analog sites, while avoiding the assumption that two locations are equivalent simply because they look similar.

The platform features an interactive globe with 15 sites of interest distributed across the world. By selecting a location, users can access information regarding its geography, geology, elevation, climate, and environmental characteristics. The platform also offers various research tools: a recommender that identifies potential matches based on selected criteria, comparison tables, an explorer for evidence and uncertainties, a laboratory for formulating research scenarios, and a case study focused on Arapey, Uruguay.

The project integrates data from services such as Open-Meteo/ERA5 (for climate data) and Macrostrat (for geological information). It also provides access to scientific resources from NASA and the USGS—including LRO, MOLA, THEMIS, HiRISE, SRTM, and Landsat—via direct links to their respective sources. The platform distinguishes between available data, hypotheses, and information that still requires verification. This distinction is crucial, as a terrestrial environment may be useful for studying a specific process without perfectly replicating the conditions found on another planet.

To develop AnalogMatch, I utilized web development technologies—primarily HTML, CSS, and JavaScript—along with Supabase to manage user accounts, research folders, and photographs. I also integrated various geographic, climate, and geological data sources, as well as a range of web design and development tools. No specialized hardware was required; the project was developed entirely using a standard computer and digital tools.

The innovation behind AnalogMatch lies in its ability to bring together geographic exploration, scientific data, and research tools within a single platform. Rather than merely displaying photographs of landscapes that resemble those on Mars or the Moon, it enables users to investigate why a potential similarity exists, what evidence supports it, and what its limitations are. Factors considered during development included data quality and provenance, scientific uncertainty, geographic coverage, ease of use, accessibility, and the platform’s scalability. I also ensured that the conclusions remained transparent and that any hypotheses generated by the system were not presented as proven scientific results.

The intended impact is to bring planetary research closer to students, educators, and those interested in space exploration, while providing a tool to organize research and highlight sites in South America—most notably Arapey, Uruguay. AnalogMatch aims to transform scattered data into opportunities for learning, making comparisons, and formulating new scientific questions.
